issues.description: dict-lookup returns #f on failure, which is indistinguishable from a key mapping to the value #f.
set-remove is recursive but not tail-recursive; may cause stack overflow on very large sets.
set-intersection is recursive but not tail-recursive; may cause stack overflow on very large sets.
dict-dissoc is recursive but not tail-recursive; may cause stack overflow on very large dictionaries.

files_reviewed.notes: Solid implementation of core functional data structures. Good use of Okasaki's queue. Performance is O(n) for many operations as they are list-based.

issues.description: vec-append and vec-set create complete copies of the state vector. Automaton construction is O(N^2) in time and space relative to the total number of pattern characters.
Lacks documentation regarding performance complexity and memory usage of the immutable vector-based construction.

files_reviewed.notes: Algorithmically correct implementation of Aho-Corasick but severely hampered by the choice of immutable vectors for the state table, leading to quadratic construction time.
Excellent test coverage for both common cases and edge cases. Includes security-focused tests for tag extraction.

summary: The data structures are well-implemented for small-scale use but lack tail-recursion in several key areas. The Aho-Corasick implementation is correct in logic but has a significant performance bottleneck in construction due to immutable vector copying. The pattern parsing tests are high quality and comprehensive.
